Title: Diagnosis of test `testHeader` failure in `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVPrinterTest`

Details:
1. The test creates a `CSVPrinter` instance using a `CSVFormat` configured with `DEFAULT`, no quote character (null), and a header `("C1", "C2", "C3")`.
2. It prints two records: `("a", "b", "c")` and `("x", "y", "z")`.
3. The test asserts the entire CSV string, expecting:
   ```
   C1,C2,C3\r\na,b,c\r\nx,y,z\r\n
   ```
4. Reviewing `CSVPrinter.printRecord(Object...)` shows it calls `print(Object)` on each value and then `println()`.
5. `println()` appends the record separator (probably `\r\n`).
6. `print(Object)` uses `print(Object, CharSequence, int, int)` which handles quoting and escaping according to `CSVFormat`.
7. `CSVFormat.withQuoteChar(Character)` when passed `null` creates a new `CSVFormat` with `quoteChar=null`, disabling quoting.
8. The CSV header was set at construction of `CSVFormat` and passed to the printer.
   
However, the actual output does not contain the header line expected at the beginning (`C1,C2,C3\r\n`).

The root cause is that just setting the header in `CSVFormat` and creating a `CSVPrinter` does not automatically print the header line. Thus the header line is missing from the output.

The test expects the header row to be automatically printed, but the current `CSVPrinter` implementation requires explicitly printing the header or skipping the header control in the format to auto-print the header. Since `CSVPrinter` does not output the header automatically, the test fails.

The fix would be in the CSVPrinter class or the interaction with CSVFormat to ensure headers are output automatically if set, or the test needs to explicitly print the headers before printing records.

Relevant methods:
- `CSVPrinter.printRecord(Object...)` (handles printing records)
- potentially constructor or initialization in `CSVPrinter` to print header
- `CSVFormat.withHeader(String...)` for setting headers

Suggested locations for fix:
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVPrinter.printRecord(java.lang.Object...)
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVPrinter.<init>(java.io.Writer,org.apache.commons.csv.CSVFormat)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
